season.evidence: Logged West Ridge ascents run Jun-Oct (Jul-Sep carry most; Oct 9, Jun 8+); web search: Mountaineers/SummitPost guidebook-derived pages give May-Sep with axe and crampons needed in the early shoulder, late October possible but short. Stored Jul-Sep kept; usable window with the one-month margin is Jun-Oct.

track.why: Logged route is West Ridge, the report walks the same line (scramble past the balanced rock from Prusik Pass, slab pitch, summit cracks, north-side rappels), summited on Sep 21, round trip from the Colchuck/Stuart trailhead lot (start/end within ~55 m of our Trailhead pin), passes the 300 m rule, summit within 14 m of Peakbagger's coordinate.

facts.text: In late September and mid-October, parties made five rappels down the north side rather than four; the stations were easy to find, one worn station can be skipped for a newer one a few feet to the side, and loose rock above the lower raps is a real hazard.
Late September: only small patches of snow remain on the north side below the rappels; passable in rock shoes
Stash your pack and poles at the base of the short scramble below the balanced rock, and carry water from the last stream near Prusik Pass, since there is none on the climb.
On the final pitch you can choose the harder right-hand crack (about 5.8) or an easier chimney to its right that passes a fixed bolt; both reach the summit ledge.

Mid-October can bring a calm, clear day with golden larches, but the rock is cold, there is a queue below the slab pitch, and the dusty, slippery top of Aasgard Pass makes the descent in the dark slow.
